newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products mostly higher, boosted by beans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products mostly higher, boosted by beans.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures were mostly higher early Friday, up in tandem with nearby soybeans, traders said.
July soybeans were higher near the open, up on ideas that Wednesday's sharp losses were overdone, traders said.
Talk that China cancelled a recent purchase of 28,000 tonnes of U.S. soyoil was seen limiting gains in soyoil futures, traders said.

USDA net export sales of soyoil of 2,000 tonnes were within the range of expectations for none to 5,000 tonnes. Net export sales of old crop soymeal were slightly above expectations and seen as supportive, traders said.
In early trade, Term Commodities and Cargill each bought 100 lots July, pit traders said.
At 1019 CDT, July soymeal was $2.00 per ton higher at $273.70 and other months were down $1.30 to $1.60 higher. July soyoil was up 0.09 cent a lb at 23.16, and other months were up 0.05 to 0.15.
